text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in ten straight games, 19 goals in that run, and became the first NHL player to record four hat tricks in one month, per Daily Faceoff. The Los Angeles Times wrote that his streak was the league's longest in 29 years when it reached nine. He leads the NHL in wins added by goals.

He's earned a lot of it. His ice time is up to 18:40 a night from 17:15, he's on the ice for 89% of Anaheim's power-play time (55% last season), and his own chances are up to 1.62 expected goals per 60 from 1.36. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.6 chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 99th percentile. That's a breakout by role and by process.

The finishing is the part that won't hold. He has 21 goals on 10.6 expected, shooting 22% against 14% last season. Even our range, built to allow for cooling, has him somewhere between 52 and 73 goals, which is its own story. One worry: at five on five the Ducks take only 45% of the expected goals with him on the ice. The power play is carrying it.
headline: Gauthier is having the month of a lifetime
